subject: Service interruption briefing, RCA and action deadlines
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Mendez <sara.mendez@fastretail.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Service interruption briefing, RCA and action deadlines

Hi Sara —

Thank you again for your patience while we investigated the degraded latency you saw on Tuesday evening (APAC/US overlap window). Attached is a concise RCA and timeline we prepared for FastRetail; key points are summarized below. We want to make sure you have clear owners, dates, and measurable mitigations.

Executive summary:
- What happened: A deployment to the serving runtime introduced a fallback path that bypassed a recently-added KV-cache integrity check for long-tail requests. Under a specific request-size distribution, that bypass caused excessive host-side work and increased P95/P99 latencies for a subset of inference calls.
- Impact: 08/03/2027 18:05–18:37 UTC — sustained P95 latency increase for your production model group (observed 400–1200ms spike for ~12% of requests). No data leakage detected; inference results were correct, just delayed.
- Root cause: A race condition in the cache population path (detailed in the attached PDF) that surfaced when concurrent request windows exceeded 6k simultaneous KV-key writes during the rollout.

Committed remediation and dates:
1) Immediate rollback: Completed 08/03/2027 18:45 UTC — prevented further regressions (done automatically by our rollback policy). Owner: runtime on-call (Connor).
2) Patch to resolve race (code + unit tests): Patch PR merged and staged to canary 08/04/2027 04:00 UTC, full rollout scheduled 08/06/2027 02:00 UTC. Owner: Aditya Rao.
3) Additional telemetry: Increase sampling for KV-cache write latencies and add alert at 95th/99th percentile. ETA: 08/05/2027. Owner: Ben Carter.
4) Customer-level guardrail: For FastRetail we will add a per-customer concurrent-write threshold and an automated slow-path that preserves latency SLOs. ETA: 08/10/2027. Owner: Marissa Cole.

Compensation: We propose a one-time service credit equal to 2 days of hosted API overage for the impacted model group; we'll apply this to your account upon your confirmation.

Attachments: redwood_rca_fastretail_20270804.pdf (PDF) — includes timeline, logs excerpts, and test reproducer; kv-cache-dump-20270804.txt (log excerpt).

Next steps I recommend:
- Quick sync: 30-minute call to review the patch plan and guardrail before rollout (available 08/05 09:00–12:00 PT).
- Confirmation of credit: Reply "confirm" and we'll schedule the credit.
- Access: If FastRetail wants the reproducer run against a sanitized version of your traffic, Connor can coordinate.

If you'd like a different remediation cadence, tell us and we'll adjust. Apologies again for the disruption — we're taking multiple layers of action to prevent recurrence.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Sara —

Short answers up front:
1) No metadata persisted outside normal operational logs; the KV dump contains key identifiers used internally for cache indexing (hashed keys). We've run a sanitization pass and the attached dump includes only hashed keys + timing fields; no client IPs or identifiable model payloads were present. The PDF includes the sanitization transcript.
2) Guardrail is server-side only. It will throttle and route to a latency-preserving slow-path for requests that exceed thresholds; no changes required to FastRetail code. We will send recommended client-side batching knobs if you want to optimize cost vs latency further.

We confirm 08/05 09:30 PT for the sync; calendar invite to follow.

Thanks — looking forward to reducing risk here.

Marissa

Subject: Re: Service interruption briefing, RCA and action deadlines

Sara / Marissa —

Wanted to add a quick technical note so your SREs have visibility ahead of the call: the race condition is in the cache population code path where two goroutines can simultaneously attempt to initialize the same cache shard. When that happens we observed a transient spike in CPU due to repeated contention and a fall-through to a synchronous write path. The synchronous path is correct functionally but increases host CPU and per-request latency.

Planned engineering mitigations: 
- Fix: atomic compare-and-swap guard + backoff to ensure only one initializer runs for a shard (unit tests + stress tests included).
- Safeguard: configurable per-tenant write-rate limiter (server-side) that prevents the synchronous fallback from triggering under normal client patterns.
- Rollout plan: merge -> 24h canary -> progressive 5% -> 25% -> 75% -> 100% conditional on latency gates.

ETA to full rollout (if gates pass): 08/06/2027 02:00 UTC. We will post incremental canary metrics to the shared drive link during rollout.

—Aditya
